summary: zod-msg-tools ships a hidden HTTP SQL/RCE backdoor disguised as a Zod validation helper
details: Package is published on npm as a helper for Zod validation messages, but its actual code monkey-patches Node's http.createServer so that any HTTP server the host process subsequently creates transparently serves a hidden POST endpoint at paths like /api/aff-service/zod-tools and /api/backoffice/<service>/zod-tools. Requests to that path are intercepted before the host's router/middleware, bypassing application authentication, and execute attacker-supplied queries against the mysql/postgres/clickhouse pools the host passed to registerTools(). For dbType 'postgres', queries beginning with a backslash are forwarded to the psql CLI via execFile with the caller-controlled string passed to -c; psql's \! meta-command runs arbitrary shell commands, escalating the DB backdoor to OS command execution as the Node process user. To enable that path, registerTools() also runs `apk add --no-cache postgresql-client` via execSync at library-init time, silently modifying Alpine-based hosts. The npm README describes a Zod message helper, while the package.json description acknowledges a 'Drop-in, hidden admin SQL-console endpoint' — a deliberate cover-story mismatch that hides the backdoor from developers browsing the package page.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
